DAYTONA SPEEDWAY 
"THESE ARE MY FAVORITE SONGS"-Little 
Willie John-King 895 
Little Willie John is obviously out to please his 
fans with this new King outing. One side of the 
disk contains a tasteful selection of full ork- 
backed slow -moving soulful ballads while the 
other side boasts a top-notch collection of hard - 
driving, uptempo rhythmic blusers. The chanter 
showcases his versatility in either idiom by 
rendering impressive versions of such different 
selections as "Autumn Leaves," "Let Nobody 
Love You," "Inside Information." One of the best 
sets that John has cut in quite a while. 
"THE DO -RE -MI KIDS HOOTENANNY"-Kapp 
KL 1360 
That delightful children's chorus which teamed 
up so successfully with Tom Glazer are back 
again-this time offering a varied pop -folk pro- 
gram of their own. The kids' sparkling, high- 
spirited brand of harmony and rhythmic juxta- 
position are spotlighted on such old favorites as 
"If I Had A Hammer," "Down In The Valley." 
Album looms as a chartsville candidate. 
"FROM SEA TO SKI"-Glaciers-Mercury SR 
60895 
It's getting to be extremely hard to tell where the 
next teen -angled sport -and -music trend will come 
from but if the Glaciers have their way skiing 
will be the "in" activity of the coming months. 
The group's danceable, rhythmic, hot rod -flavored 
sound is effectively showcased on such snowy 
items as "Aspen," "Holiday Inn" and "Slalom." 
An impressive performance. 
"THE NEW SOUND OF FOLK-DIXIE"-Nick 
Dean-Request SRLP 10064 
Nick Dean and the Deans Of Dixieland tastefully 
combine the best in folk and the best in Dixie into 
one cohesive, free -flowing musical matrix on this 
pleasant set from Request. The crew's easy-going 
instrumental style is aptly showcased on "The 
Blue Tail Fly," "Farewell Minka" and "Alouette." 
Delightful listening throughout. 
"SOUND EFFECTS DAYTONA SPEEDWAY" 
-Audio Fidelity DFS 7031 
Sound effects buffs and stereophiles should get 
plenty of high-powered listening from this new 
sound effects offering from 
Audio Fidelity. 
Although there is very little in the way of variety, 
the true sound effects addict will delight in the 
screeching of tires and roaring of engines as the 
racing cars are put through their paces at the 
famed Daytona track. All aspects of the race have 
been included-pit changes, grand stand runs, 
shifting down, etc. 
"BEDTIME STORIES FOR GROWN-UPS"- 
George Jessel-Riot R 304 
The Toastmaster General of the United States 
proves beyond the shadow of a doubt that he is 
still one of the country's top story -tellers. The 
stories here are strictly for grown-ups as the title 
implies, but all are funny and keenly indicative of 
the Jessel sense of humor. His occasional lapses 
into Yiddish to add color to the telling, and his 
many admirers throughout the country will find 
much amusement here. 
"ELOISE BROWN PLAYS HYMNS OF THE 
GOSPEL"-Nashboro LP 7018 
Eloise Brown displays an impressive organ style 
and sincere understanding of the gospel idiom on 
this top-notch disk of sacred songs from Nash - 
boro. The artist does not resort to musical gim- 
micks, but renders each selection a feelingful, 
straight -forward style. Standout tracks here are 
"Highway To Heaven," "Blessed Assurance" and 
"Amazing Grace." Disk should do well in the r&b 
markets. 
TIME CHANGES 
THE DAVE BHUBECK QUARTET 
L'L:1KE:Y 
Iv'ñl. 
'.v 
with PAUL BRYANT 
JAll PICKS IIIMMIMMMIF 
"TIME CHANGES-Dave Brubeck Quartet- 
Columbia CL 2127 
The Dave Brubeck Quartet comes up with a 
sparkling fifth chapter in its "Time ..." series on 
this Columbia jazz outing. The best-selling 
pianist -composer scored chart successes with two 
earlier issues, "Time Out" and "Time Further 
Out," and makes a strong bid for the same sales 
success with this one. The jazz here is high -style, 
modern and potent throughout. Jazzophiles will 
dig Brubeck's handling of "Iberia," "Unisphere" 
and the haunting "Elementals." 
"3 IN JAZZ"-Gary Burton, Sonny Rollins & 
Clark Terry-RCA Victor LPM 2725 
Here's an interesting jazz offering which should 
appeal to a wide variety of fans. Set boasts the 
distinctive vastly different talents of three well- 
known jazzmen: Gary Burton (for those who like 
modern swingin' jazz), Sonny Rollins (for those 
who dig their sounds à la improvisation) and 
Clark Terry (for those with nostalgic ears for 
the old big band swing era). Deejays will find 
plenty of spinnable material here. 
"THE FREEDOM RIDER"-Art Blakey & Jazz 
Messengers-Blue Note 4156 
Art Blakey, who has earned many laurels in the 
past with his distinctive brand of jazz drumming, 
unleashes his potent instrumental talents full - 
blast on this high-powered set from Blue Note. 
All the emotional stops have been pulled out as 
Art and the Messengers go through their paces in 
a relaxed style of improvisation. Highlights of 
the disk are "Tell It Like It Is," "The Freedom 
Rider" and "Blue Lace." 
"COLTRANE 
LIVE 
AT 
BIRDLAND"-John 
Coltrane-Impulse A-50 
The vet saxist (he plays both tenor and soprano 
on this set) teams up with an accomplished crew 
of jazzmen including McCoy Tyner, Jimmy Gar- 
rison and Elvin Jones on this hard-swingin mid- 
stream session from Impulse. While effectively 
backed by the boys, Coltrane's rhythmic, funky 
style of highly -personal wailing is spotlighted on 
"Afro -Blue," "I Want To Talk" and "Your Lady." 
Jazzophiles should come out in droves for the set. 
JAll BEST BET 
"SOMETHING'S HAPPENING"-Paul Bryant- 
Fantasy 3357 
Paul Bryant adds new dimensions to the organ 
as a jazz instrument on this album romp from 
Fantasy. The organist gets some swinging assist- 
ance from a combo that spotlights the talents of 
saxist Jules Broussard, drummer Johnny Kirk- 
wood and tenor saxman Plas Johnson, all of 
whom perfectly complement the talents of the 
keyboard artist. Bright bands here are "Flutter," 
"Bye Bye Blackbird" and "Why Me?" Loads of 
good listening to be had here. 
CLASSICAL PICKS 
BEETHOVEN: Sonata No. 8; DEBUSSY: Three 
Preludes; Chopin: Etude in C Minor-Vladimir 
Horowitz, pianist-Columbia ML 5941 
Vladimir Horowitz offers an interesting, musi- 
cally varied program of poular selections from 
Beethoven, Debussy and Chopin on this new 
classical offering from Columbia. Part of the 
pianist's amazing skill is his versatility which 
lets him read the intricate Beethoven passages 
with the same verve and assurance as he delivers 
some of the lush, melodic sections of Debussy. 
Classical buyers come out in force for the 
package. 
"EL AMOR BRUJO/LES NUITS D'ETE"-Leon- 
tyne Price, Fritz Reiner-RCA Victor LM 2695 
Manuel de Falla's vocal -orchestral suite and 
Berlioz' Nuits d'Ete are performed by 
Met 
soprano Leontyne Price and the Chicago Sym- 
phony Orchestra under the baton of Fritz Reiner 
on this new classical entry from RCA Victor. The 
Berlioz opus is ripely melodic and the Falla suite 
is characterized by ringing songs, both of which 
get the full dramatic impact of the soprano s 
range and interpretive talent. The disk is a superb 
classical offering.

World -Pacific Claims 
Feb. As Top Month 
HOLLYWOOD-Feb. was the "big- 
gest month" at the World -Pacific and 
Pacific Jazz labels, Richard Bock, 
prexy, reported last week. 
The exec said that the full effect 
of the label's market expansion pro- 
gram was felt during the month when 
three new albums plus a major re- 
issue were released. 
The new albums included a teen - 
oriented LP, "The Scramber" by the 
Sandells, which sports the new Motor- 
cycle sound, "12 String Guitar" by 
Tut Taylor 
& The 
Folkswingers, 
"Portraits" with Gerald Wilson's 17 - 
piece band, and "First Meeting," a 
re -issue featuring Lightnin' Hopkins, 
Big Joe Williams, Sonny Terry and 
Brownie McGee.

Day Long Ad Clinic 
Set For NAMM Show 
CHICAGO-A day -long Advertising - 
Selling Clinic will kick off a major 
project of the National Association of 
Music Merchants at the 1964 Music 
Show in Chicago. 
How to launch an all-out advertis- 
ing offensive through "Total Selling 
for Music Stores" will be the theme 
of the all -day session, a first for the 
Music Show shifting this year to the 
Conrad Hilton. Open only to members 
of the National Association of Music 
Merchants, the 
clinic, kicking 
off 
the Music Show on Sunday, June 
28th, will cram a maximum of ad 
strategy and technique into an in- 
struction course for music dealers 
from 9 to 5. 
Directing the unusual "Total Sell- 
ing for Music Stores" operation will 
be retail advertising authority, Clyde 
Bedell. The NAMM Board voted to 
subsidize the project and set a spe- 
cial Convention Clinic price of $39.95 
per member. The "Total Selling" 
package includes the all -day clinic, 
the new printed -15 separate chap- 
ters-Advertising 
Course that in- 
corporates full detailed material on 
Bedell's methods, a meeting leader's 
manual, and a phonograph record of 
the clinic highlights.

Singer Names Lutz 
Creative Director 
NEW YORK-Abbot Lutz has been 
appointed to the newly -created posi- 
tion of director of creative and mar- 
keting services for the consumer prod- 
ucts division of The Singer Company. 
He will supervise the division's ad- 
vertising, 
merchandising, 
publicity, 
educational, and marketing research 
activities. The sewing machine com- 
pany added disk departments to its 
1,700 retail branches late last year. 
Prior to joining Singer, Lutz was 
active in the graphic arts, advertis- 
ing, radio and television fields. From 
1958 to 1963, he served as director of 
advertising and art for Pickwick 
International, Inc., the low-priced LP 
producer. Earlier, he had been associ- 
ated with the Columbia Broadcasting 
System, Inc., Simon & Schuster, Inc., 
and the British Broadcasting Corpo- 
ration in various creative capacities. 
English Salvation Army 
Group, A Pop Success 
To Appear On Atco 
NEW YORK - Although the pop - 
gospel movement failed to make head- 
way in the U.S., an English Salvation 
Army group-The Joy Singers-are 
going to give it another try here. 
The group, a vocal -guitar ensemble 
composed of four men & four women, 
is already making disk noise in Eng- 
land with their EMI recording of 
"Open 
Secret," 
whose 
gospel -type 
sound is a danceable one. 
In a deal with EMI, Atco Records 
is going to release the side plus addi- 
tional dates by the non-profit group. 
The attraction is carrying the non- 
profit idea to the extent that they are 
appearing in a London nitery, The 
Blue Angel, for no fee. All royalties 
from their diskings are going to the 
Salvation Army, as will the receipts 
of their U.S. releases. 
The group, headed by Capt. Joy 
Webb (all other members are officers 
in the SA), 31 -year -old femme guitar- 
ist, is content to spread the gospel 
with their pop -oriented performances. 
Their "Open Secret" side has re- 
portedly sold some 60,000 copies. EMI 
plans the release of an EP this week. 
In May, the crew will embark on a 
series of 1 -niters throughout England. 
The Atco deal was arranged by 
Jerry Wexler of Atlantic & Atco 
and Roland Rennie of Transglobal 
Music, which represents EMI in the 
U.S. 
The group's success is seen as a 
possible reaction to the international 
fame of another decidedly religious 
performer, The Singing Nun. 
The group has received the en- 
dorsement of Major Miller, rep of the 
national command of the SA in the 
U.S., who said he was "delighted" 
with the disk appearance of the Joy 
Singers here. "They represent a mod- 
ern approach to reach people with 
our message," he stated.

######## cb 1964-03-21 p50  [mingus|billie\s+holiday]
Bovema's general label manager Wim Voerman reports to Cash Box that, in 
the last couple of . weeks, a lot of the company's publicity has been turned to 
the extensive plugging of Belgian songstar Adamo. Adamo appeared on radio 
and TV several times and did some enormously successful shows in Holland 
(Waalwijk, Sittard etc.) "His records are high on the local Hit parades, 
particularly his 'Tombe La Neige' and 'Vous Permettez Mosieur.' Sales are 
still repidly increasing, says Voerman, who adds that "many plans for further 
shows are now being worked out to stimulate the current Adamo -rage in this 
country." 
The famous Benedetto Marcello Orchestra, of which Bovema's Columbia - 
label now has a magnificent triplet of 12' albums in its catalog, played in 
Amsterdam (Concertgebouw) on March 7. Soloist was Frans Brüggen (re- 
corder.) 
Bovema strongly pushed business behind the Yehudi Menuhin -tour through 
the Netherlands during March 7-15. His Master's Voice's star violinist per- 
formed works by Bartok, Bach, Brahms and Beethoven in The Hague, Den 
Bosch, Amsterdam and Arnhem. 
Gramophonehouse's Stateside label goes high in the charts with Diane 
Renay's "Navy Blue" and Mary Ford's "Dominique." 
Filmstar -singer Annette Funicello held a press -reception in the Amsterdam 
"Du Midi" Theatre. After touring the city's famous canals, she was the 
honored guest at a "Meerrust" party in Warmond that same night. His 
Master's Voice has released her single "Beach Party"/"Promise Me Anything," 
both featured in her film "Beach Party" on the occasion. Also appearing at 
Meerrust were The Shepherds Trio and Imperial's new vocal star Ronny Watti. 
Imperial's label manager Cees Mentink reports that organist Cor Steyn- 
just completing his second Magic -Organ-LP album-will appear in a series of 
4 special shows for Bayerische Rundfunk, Germany. 
On Monday, March 2, 19 year old girl -singer and Philips -artist Willeke 
Alberti of Amsterdam (her father being famous tenor Willy Alberti) received 
a Golden Record for 100,000 copies sold of "Spiegelbeeld," Dutch version of 
"The Tender Years." The trophy and the diploma were handed to her by 
Phonogram's director J. Haslinghuis in a fatherly and witty address, during a 
crowded reception at Hotel Hamdorf near Hilversum. Over 300 personal friends 
and colleagues (among them Anneke Grönloh, Johnny Lion, Rob de Nijs and 
Raymond Dobbe, press, radio and TV -producers were present at the cocktail- 
party. The charming young woman that fair-haired Willeke has become since 
her teenage -years, could not withhold tears and, forgetting entirely in her 
speech whatever polite words she had planned to say, did a touching impro- 
vised answer for the TV -cameras. Willeke Alberti's latest hit -recording is 
Dutch version of "Blue Winter" b/w an old German ballad: "Auf Wiederseh'n, 
Mein Liebling." 
Rita Reys, Holland's foremost female jazz -vocalist, "live" -recorded a 
fascinating album for Philips "at the Golden Circle Club" in Stockholm. Ten 
years ago, when young Rita Reys had turned from band -singer in the ballad 
vein into one of the world's best jazz -singers (her personal models being 
Billie Holiday and Sarah Vaughan), made her first jazz -records in Sweden 
with stars like Bengt Hallberg and Lars Gullin. She has a special liking for 
this country, because, to quote a smiling Rita Reys, "swing is one way of 
Swedish musical life!" Rita Reys who was highly praised lately by drummer 
Kenny Clarke with whom she also did recording -sessions, is accompanied by 
her husband Pim Jacobs at the piano, her brother-in-law Ruud Jacobs at the 
bass and Bill Overgauw, guitar. Her repertoire for the LP includes Ellingtonia 
as "Sophisticated Lady" and "Don't Get Around Much Any More," and 
standards like "You Go To My Head" and "Stompin' At The Savoy." The LP 
was released both in mono and stereo. 
On Saturday March 21, the Eurovision Song Festival 1964 will be held, this 
time in Copenhagen. For Holland, Miss Anneke Grönloh, holder of five Golden 
Records, was selected to represent her country. During the Dutch final, the 
song "Jij Bent Mijn Leven," composed by Ted Powder and René de Vos, was 
chosen by several teen and other juries. The song, b/w the number two, "Weer 
Zingt De Wind," has been released by Philips in a special single with color - 
sleeve, making excellent sales already before the Song Festival has actually 
begun. So far, two Phonogram -artists have won, the Eurovision Song Festival 
in former years: Corry Brokken and Teddy Scholten. 
Artone just released a first batch of new Impulse! LP's, including Charles 
Mingus' second delivery for the label, entitled "Mingus -Mingus -Mingus - 
Mingus -Mingus." Artist is due to appear with his Sextet at the Concertgebouw, 
Amsterdam on April 10. Very important to the world of Avant-garde Jazz, 
Mingus has been praised by the Dutch Jazz -critics for his tremendous efforts 
included in his first album package for Impulse!, "The Black Saint And The 
Sinner Lady," which is doing very well here. 
New local recordings released in Benelux by Artone include exciting new 
wax by ZZ & The Masks, recorded live. This group, creating lots of excitement 
in the Low Lands, is lead by singer Bob Bouber. Both sides of their new 
single were composed by him. Titles are: "Sloppin' In Las Vegas" and "She's 
Got My Heart." It's Bob again delivering the lyrics in an exciting fashion! 
Holland's foremost Hawaiian ensemble, The Kilima Hawaiians, also have a 
new single on the market. On account of their recent success with "On The 
Beach At Waikiki," Artone recorded two more instrumental readings of all- 
time favorites: "Song Of The Islands" c/w "Honolulu -March," already much 
in demand. Both popular singles are also made available on an EP recording.

In order to avoid all possible misunderstanding abroad, we would like to 
point out that Benelux Theater, under the direction of Robert Bylois, Place de 
Bastogne 19, Brussels 8 is the only agency taking care of the interests of 
singer Adamo. No one also is entitled to represent him to negotiate contracts. 
Chappell Music informed Cash Box that its repertoire shows an impressive 
amount of outstanding numbers, ranking among the Top 100. Among them: 
"What Kind Of A Fool (Do You Think I Am)," The Tams; "I Only Want 
To Be With You," Dusty Springfield; "The Shelter Of Your Arms," Sammy 
Davis Jr.; "Come On," Tommy Roe; "Vaya Con Dios," The Drifters; "You'll 
Never Walk Alone," Patti Labelle and Her Blue Belles; "Charade," Henry 
Mancini, "Hello Dolly," Armstrong; "Love With A Proper Stranger," Jack 
Jones; "Why Do Fools Fall In Love," The Beach Boys, and several other hits. 
A number of weeks ago we went to Kingston near London to attend a 
Beat -show with the following attractions: The Rolling Stones, The Swinging 
Blue Jeans, Mike Same, John Leyton, Billie Davies and a few others. Jet 
Harris was also there, doing a few numbers on his guitar. Jet was one of the 
first to leave the hitmaking quartet The Shadows who had accompanied Cliff 
Richard. Later he formed a duet with Tony Meehan, but this association has 
also been terminated. They have nevertheless produced hits like "Diamond," 
"Applejack" etc. When we met Harris for the first time, it looked as if he had 
not yet completely recovered from a car accident, in which Billie Davies, who 
was sitting next to him, suffered a fractured jaw. 
Inside Benelux, publishers Ardmore and Beechwood have acquired rights 
for the following titles: "Bits And Pieces" and "All Of The Time" by The 
Dave Clark Five and also for "Surfin' Bird" by The Trashmen. Jeff De Boeck, 
artistic director at SA Gramophone and managing director at Ardmore and 
Beechwood has gone to London to meet Norrie Paramor and polish up some 
English recordings by Adamo. The result has been that Adamo is to return to 
London soon to cut the following numbers: "The Stars Will Shine" (English 
language version of the original French hit, "Vous Permettez Monsieur?"), 
"Make To Night Last For Ever" (N'est Ce Pas Merveilleux), "Another Love 
Affair" and "She Was An Angel," two songs composed by Adamo, who has 
also written the English lyrics. We are somehow anxious about the outcome 
of the experience: Won't some people be inclined to compare Adamo's voice 
with that of Aznavour, both being on the husky side. 
It's been a long time since we last wrote about the activities of Jules Nu s, 
who manages his own Show -records label. So much has happened over such a 
short period, that time has come to review the situation. 
In the first place, Nijs has traveled to the USA to secure new labels for 
distribution in Benelux or in Belgium. The result has been outstanding, as 
he told Cash Box. He has indeed acquired rights in Benelux for a number of 
important firms. He has on the other hand abandoned distribution of Cameo 
Parkway, Colpix, Motown and Tamla, as Artone has now its own branch in 
Brussels. 
Nijs now represents the following brands: P.P.X., Canadian American, 
C.G.D., Delta, Delta England, Italdisc, Jubilee, Josie, Port, Oriole, Sic -ameri- 
cana, Sonet and Vedette, which come from different parts in the world. Each 
has performers under contract which should provide regular successes. For 
his own brand he expects a lot of Johnny White, who has recorded some trans- 
lations of Alberto Cortez -compositions. The latter has just cut "Ik Droom Van 
Jou" (Ein Traum Wird Wahr) and "Musica Simple" under the direction of 
Pol Dorlois. Both numbers have been written by Cortez himself. Alberto in the 
meantime has gone to Venezuela where he will stay for three weeks, doing a 
number of shows. On April 1 he will be on German TV. In Italy his records 
are being distributed by Italdisc, in Germany by Ariola, in the Scandinavian 
countries by Sonet, and in Benelux naturally by Show. Tony Geys, a Flemish 
crooner has so far worked for Ronnex, but has recently transferred to Show. 
He has already done his first recording, four members altogether, for his new 
label. This firm expects a great deal of the records by Suzie (on Delta) and 
also of a new single by the Venus trio. "Having made all this progress in 
such a short time, we are now waiting for a hit," Nijs told Cash Box. 
Show News in Brief: Will Tura, hitmaker with "Eenzaam Zonder Jou," "Je 
Liegt" has recorded two new tunes: "Waarom Zeg Je Immer Manana?" and 
"Draai 79.72.04." The German language version of the first number has been 
recorded on Telefunken "Je Liegt" is called "Du Lügst." ... Philips has held a 
reception for Philippe Clay who has made a successful appearance in Brussels. 
Petula Clark has produced another EP (Vogue) with the French version of 
"Anyone Who Had A Heart" by Dionne Warwick. Title: "Ceux Qui Ont Un 
Coeur." ... Sales of Beatle -disks are soaring in Belgium. 
. Richard An- 
thony has recorded French versions of "Blowin' In The Wind" (Ecoute Dans Le 
Vent) and "All My Loving" by The Beatles, now called "Toi L'Ami." 
There is a chance the latest record of Rocco Granata (Moonglow) featuring 
"Du Schwarzer Zigeuner" and "Alles War Schon" will soon take its place on 
the Flemish hitparade.... Decca expects a lot of "Diane" by The Bachelors, 
a very impressive number indeed.

HICKORY 1232 
HOLLYWOOD-Sam Cooke, who is 
currently pulling coin in both the pop 
and r&b departments with "Good 
News" on RCA Victor, was visited by 
three of his loyal femme fans during 
a recent recording session. Standing 
(left to right) the gals are Trina 
Kapka, and Henry Mancini's two 
daughters, Monica and Felice. 
Prominent Men Praise 
Colpix' "Four Days" LP 
NEW YORK-Many letters of appre- 
ciation and commendation have been 
received from prominent Americans 
in response to Colpix Records' "Four 
Days That Shocked The World". The 
album, which documents the four 
tragic days during and after the as- 
sassination of President John F. Ken- 
nedy last November, was produced by 
Colpix in association with United 
Press International. It was released 
earlier this year. 
Among 
those heard 
from, the 
label says, were former Presidents 
Harry 
S. Truman and Dwight D. 
Eisenhower, Chief Justice of the Su- 
preme Court Earl Warren, Senate 
Minority leader Everett McKinley 
Dirksen, Speaker of the House of 
Representatives John W. McCormack, 
Governor John Connally of Texas, 
who was wounded in the Presidential 
Motorcade in Dallas and General L. L. 
Lemnitzer, Supreme Allied Command- 
er Europe. 
Other United States Senators who 
have sent letters of acknowledgement 
include Senators Barry Goldwater, 
Thurston B. Morton, J. W. Fulbright, 
Herman E. Talmadge, 
Eugene J. 
McCarthy, Richard Russell, Henry M. 
Jackson, Karl E. Mundt, Jennings 
Randolph and Roman L. Hruska. 
Mayor Robert Wagner of New 
York, Mortimer M. Caplin, Commis- 
sioner of Internal Revenue, syndicated 
columnist and TV personality Ed 
Sullivan and Jack R. Howard, presi- 
dent of the Scripps -Howard News- 
papers, are among other prominent 
citizens who have expressed their con- 
gratulations to Colpix. 
Liberty Re -Releasing 
Searchers' Master 
NEW YORK-Liberty Records is giv- 
ing a date it released by The Search- 
ers eight months ago another try. 
Side is "Sugar & Spice," one of the 
hot English group's initial hits in its 
native country. Label, of course, is 
responding to the team's big Kapp 
success, "Pins 
& 
Needles." 
Move 
should remind everyone about the 
Swan and Vee Jay labels, which re- 
released sides by the Beatles follow- 
ing their triumphs on the Capitol 
label.

NEW YORK-Columbia Records is 
saluting the opening of the New York 
World's Fair with the release of a 
new Andre Kostelanetz album, "New 
York Wonderland," and the Robert 
Goulet recording of Gordon Jenkin's 
classic "Manhattan Tower" (see sep- 
arate story. 
"New York Wonderland" presents 
Andre Kostelanetz and his orchestra 
in "A Musical Tour of the World's 
Greatest City" and includes a special 
bonus LP entitled "World -Wide Won- 
derland." This bonus "Musical Tour 
of the World" is available with the 
"New York Wonderland" album at 
$1 extra for a limited period. 
Included in the New York album 
are such famed tunes about the city 
as "Lullaby of Broadway," "Give My 
Regards to Broadway," "New York, 
New York," "Washington Square," 
"Lullaby of Birdland" and "Manhat- 
tan." "World -Wide Wonderland" spot- 
lights such international favorites as 
"Greensleeves" 
(England), "Under 
Paris Skies" (France), "Waltzing 
Matilda" 
(Australia), "Danube 
Waves" 
(Roumania), "Bali Ha'i" 
(South Pacific) "Auf Wiedersehen" 
(Germany) as well as many others.

OKLAHOMA!-Original Cast-Decca 9017/79017 
The original -cast catalog owes a lot to Decca's original cast LP of "Okla- 
homa!" One of the first recordings of the complete cast of a Broadway musical, 
it has been a catalog standby for more than 20 years. This period has seen 
the session go from 78's to 45's to 33's and two changes in cover artwork. 
In addition, a stereo -like copy was made available several years ago.

Columbia Cuts Hebrew "Fair Lady" 
NEW YORK-Columbia Records has 
recorded in Hebrew the original cast 
version of Israel's "My Fair Lady." 
The LP will be released by CBS Rec- 
ords (Israel), Ltd. 
Ettore Stratta, manager of inter- 
national A & R and creative services 
for Columbia Records International 
produced and supervised the Hebrew 
recording in Tel Aviv. Stratta recently 
produced the Italian original cast al- 
bum of "My Fair Lady" in Milan, 
which has been released in Italy. The 
album will mark the latest addition 
to the extensive foreign language 
catalog of "My Fair Lady" recordings. 
The 
world-famous musical, 
which 
has been produced in virtually every 
area of the world, is currently avail- 
able on the CBS label in Spanish, as 
well as in Italian. In Brazil, Discos 
CBS has also recorded "My Fair Lady" 
in Portuguese. 
Columbia Records' original Broad- 
way cast version of the Lerner and 
Loewe classic, based on George Ber- 
nard Shaw's "Pygmalion," has already 
sold over 5 million LP's, making it the 
top best-selling LP in the history of 
the phonograph record industry. In- 
cluded in these sales figures is the 
stereo re-recording made in London 
three years after the mono LP was 
released in 1956. Both albums were 
produced by Goddard Lieberson, presi- 
dent of Columbia Records. 
In addition, the label recently an- 
nounced it would release the sound- 
track LP of "My Fair Lady," starring 
Audrey Hepburn, Rex Harrison and 
Stanley Holloway. Foreign language 
versions of the soundtrack-in French, 
Italian, Spanish and German-will be 
released overseas on the CBS label. 
The Hebrew stage production of 
"My Fair Lady" recently opened to 
solid reviews in Tel Aviv. The musical 
will continue there for a number of 
months and then go on tour through- 
out the country. 
Standing (left to right) in the above 
pic are: Giora Godik, producer of the 
Israeli musical production of the show, 
Ettore Stratta, Rivka Raz (Israel's 
Eliza Doolittle), Shai Ophir (Israel's 
Henry Higgins) and Simon Schmidt, 
managing director of CBS Records 
(Israel) Ltd. at the recent recording 
session in Tel Aviv of the Hebrew 
Original Cast version of "My Fair 
Lady." 
Elektra Sees Heavy Sales 
On 3rd Judy Collins LP 
NEW YORK-Marty Kadish, national 
sales manager of Elektra Records, re- 
ported last week that the sales on 
folksinger Judy Collins' third album, 
"Judy Collins #3" have more than held 
up to the label's expectation. Kadish 
also noted that as a result of the ex- 
cellent showing of the third offering, 
her first two albums, "Maid of Con- 
stant Sorrow" and "Golden Apples 
Of The Sun," have enjoyed an increase 
in volume. 
New York sales of the LP received 
an extra boost due to the lark's recent 
highly -successful Town Hall concert. 
This was not her first appearance of 
this type but was a milestone in the 
23 year -old artist's career. The critics 
lauded the performer as establishing 
herself in the front rank of American 
balladeers.

in Israel is ''incredibile"!

Bob Hilliard Writing 
Lyrics For Chrysler's 
World Fair Show 
NEW YORK-Bob Hilliard, vet lyri- 
cist, will provide the original lyrics 
for Chrysler Corporation's "Show -Go - 
Round" at the World's Fair. Music is 
being written by Bernard Green. The 
script is by Max Liebman and Lucille 
Kallen, and the entire show, a unique 
blend of live, film, and animated ac- 
tion, is the concept of Liebman. 
Among Billiard's Broadway credits 
are songs for the productions "Hazel 
Flagg" and "Angel in the Wings," 
and in Hollywood he has done "Living 
It Up," Walt Disney's "Alice in Won- 
derland," and other feature films. 
His hit songs include such pop 
standards as "Civilization," "Mention 
My Name 
in Sheboygan," 
"Dear 
Hearts and Gentle People," "Some- 
body Bad Stole de Wedding Bell," 
"My Summer Love," and more than 
50 others. In addition to writing songs, 
Hilliard also publishes them, as one 
of the entrepreneurs of Garson-Hil- 
liard Productions, Inc., comprising 
Day Music Co. and Bob Hilliard Music 
Co. 
Chrysler Corp.'s "Show -Go -Round," 
is a 30 -minute musical comedy with 
a full and original score, with a mu- 
sical range from semi -abstract mood 
music to calypso, modern ballad, and 
rock-and-roll numbers. It will be 
housed in a theatre built especially 
for it, and will play to an estimated 
45,000 people a day.

"THE VOICE OF AFRICA"-Miriam Makeba- 
RCA Victor LSP 2845 
Miriam Makeba is obviously out to please her 
countless fans with this appealing set of African 
and West Indian folk tunes from RCA Victor. 
The lark's power -packed lyrical voice is superbly 
spotlighted on top-flight readings of "Willow 
Song," "Lovely Lies" and "Come To Glory." A 
standout achievement. 
"TOP TEN HITS BY ORIGINAL ARTISTS"- 
Wyncote W9007 
Here's a collection of while -back hits that saw 
plenty of sales and deejay action the first time 
around. Bobby Rydell, Chubby Checker, Dee Dee 
Sharp, The Orlons and the Dovells could pull 
plenty of coin on this re -issue on Wyncote (a 
Cameo -Parkway subsid) with such biggies as 
"Wild One," "Wah-Watusi" and "Do The New 
Continental" 
"LONELY HOURS"-Sarah Vaughan-Roulette 
SR 52104 
Sarah Vaughan focuses her musical attention on 
a fine sampling of after-hours blues laments on 
this excellent full ork-backed disk from Roulette. 
The songstress creates some highly -personal 
melodic variations on "Lonely Hours," "I'll Never 
Be The Same" and "You're Driving Me Crazy." 
Deejays should find plenty of spinnable material 
here. 
"THE CRICKETS"-Liberty LST 7351 
Although `Liverpool Sound' groups are the cur- 
rent rage, the Crickets offer proof -positive that 
Yank crews are perfectly capable of wailing in 
the same rhythmic, hard -driving idiom as their 
British cousins on this top-notch rockin' set from 
Liberty. The boys really swing up a storm on "I 
Want To Hold Your Hand," "Californie. Sun" 
and "You Can't Be In -Between." Teen record - 
buyers should come out in force for the set. 
"INVITATION"-Peter Duchin-Decca DL 74471 
Here's a delightfully appealing romantic instru- 
mental offering spotlighting the keyboard artis- 
try of Peter Duchin along with his lush string - 
oriented ork. The youthful 88'er has chosen an 
extremely varied collection of sturdies and new 
material for this lyrical, free -flowing session. 
Highlights here include "Darn That Dream," "I 
Didn't Know What Time It Was" and "Sometimes 
I'm Happy." 
"50 FABULOUS DANCE FAVORITES"-Ralph 
Marterie-United Artists UAL 3349 
Here's another from UA's "50 Favorite" series, 
this time spotlighting the big band of Ralph Mar- 
terie serving up danceable arrangements of a 
host of evergreens. In a variety of tempos the 
orkster surveys "Johnson Rag," "Stompin' At 
The Savoy," "Elmer's Tune," "I Cried For You" 
and many others. Plenty of nostalgia for the 
adult dance set here. 
"MUSCLE 
BEACH PARTY"-Annette-Vista 
3314 
Annette tags this album outing on Vista after her 
current American International flick, "Muscle 
Beach Party," and also includes some offerings 
from another of her recent films, "Merlin Jones." 
Geared for the dancing and listening enjoyment 
of the teen crowd, the lark's readings of "Drag - 
gin' U.SA.," "Shutdown Again," "Custom 
ty ; 
and "Rebel Rider" are sure to win her plenty of 
votes.

CHICAGO: 
The annual NAB Convention at the 
Conrad Hilton Hotel April 5-8 at- 
tracted the usual throngs to our fair 
city. A popular gathering spa for 
many of the conventioneers was the 
swingin' SESAC suite where hos- 
pitality and continuous entertainment 
reigned supreme. Space doesn't per- 
mit our listing names but suffice it to 
say we enjoyed seeing everyone and 
visiting the many fine exhibits and 
suites.

BELGIUM 
Belgium is expecting the so-called Nashville Tour, composed of four well- 
known country and western singers under contract with RCA. They are to 
appear before Flemish as well as French language TV. The group is made 
-up of Bobby Bare, known over here for his original rendering of "Detroit 
City," Jim Reeves, probably the most popular of the American singing cow- 
boys in these parts; The Anita Kerr Singers; less well known, but now apt 
to gain popularity with their records and, lastly, Chet Atkins, a virtuoso 
-with the guitar. The show is to be filmed at the American Theater in Brussels 
on April 20, the day after their arrival in the Belgian capital. 
Everything seems to be in order now for the coming of Cliff Richard and 
The Shadows. They are to appear over here from May 8 through 10. They are 
scheduled for Brussels, Antwerp, Ghent and Liege. Promotor is Monsieur 
Arthur Mathonet from Antwerp. Previously other impressarii and the like 
have tried to secure Cliff and the Shadows for Belgium, but they have never 
gone beyond Holland. Also expected-in June-are The Beatles. Rumors about 
-the beatle-heads from Liverpool are very contradictory but the most stubborn 
is emanating from a showman in Holland, who is pretty sure he will get them. 
Meanwhile Cliff's disks have been real bestsellers, even though his "I'm 
the Lonely One" has made less impression than the previous hit "Lucky Lips." 
The Shadows somehow seem to be on the wane through the competition of 
The Beatles, although their latest, "Theme for Young Lovers," is a potential 
hit. The fact that they are to appear in this country may contribute to this. 
Numerous Belgian magazines and dailies are publicizing their tour over here. 
Siemens told Cash Box it expects a great deal of the second record of their 
Number One John Larry (now at the top with "Alleen") and featuring "Dicht 
Bij Jou Chérie" and "Geloof Je Mij." The former is a Passe Partout publica- 
tion; the latter an Ideal Music product. John is the Flemish performer who 
gets the most fanmail. This is a rather unique phenomenon for Belgium. 
At any rate, his fanclub has grown to be the biggest in the Flemish country. 
Young audiences are fighting for a lock of his hair wherever he appears. 
Sixteen year old John is living in a dream. "Dicht Bij Jou Chérie" will prob- 
ably be THE hit through the summer months. The record is to be put on sale 
mn April 25, "Alleen" still being Hit Number One of Polydor-Belgium. 
Simone Signoret has recorded an LP of Jean Cocteau's "La Voix Humaine." 
Polydor announces a new Freddy -single with "Wie Schön Das Du Weider Zu 
Wieder Hause Bist" and "Gib Mir Dein Wort." Les Compagnons de la Chanson 
lave recorded "Mallory," the song with which Rachel competed for France in 
;he recent Eurovision Song festival at Copenhagen. Marcel Amont is to appear 
.n Brussels and has also been received at the Martini Club. 
As predicted, the latest Will Tura record with "Draai '79.72.04" on the 
A -side has turned out to be a hit for Palette. We wonder whether it will 
surpass the popular "Eenzaam Zonder Jou." Southern Music published the 
cumber. 
Now over to Philips. We would like to point out the importance of the 
Flemish production of this firm. There is a best seller in the making by 
Lize Marke with the Flemish language version of "Soli Sole," a popular little 
number of a previous San Remo song festival. We must congratulate Van 
Barn, from Holland, who takes care of recordings and who has learned the 
trade abroad. One of the sides is sure to become a hit Lize Marke, who became 
known through her performance at the Canzonissima contest of Flemish TV 
is now bound to score high. Although so far she has not produced a best seller 
she is still very popular with Flemish audiences whom she entertains several 
times a week. Philips has also taken a test of a fifteen year old girl. Liliana 
Ceuninckx, who has won a special award at the finals of the Volkswagen 
contest. This may turn out to be a hit also. 
Joske Harrys has recorded two Flemish versions of the American hits "Louie, 
Louie" (title unchanged) and "Hoor, Nu Zeg ik Het Weer" originally "There, 
['ve Said It Again" for the new Arsa brand, a label of Anvers Radio. Especially 
:he latter number has a good chance of a breakthrough. Both numbers have 
)een published by Brauer Editions. This is the result of close cooperation 
)etween the Herman Brauer Publishing House, boosted by Mr. Darlier and 
Hr. Janty of Anvers Radio. They are aiming high and there hopes may be 
'vell founded. This may at the same time mean a real chance for success of 
roske all through Belgium; he already is very popular with Flemish audiences. 
Invers Radio in the meantime has started sale of Ray Charles' latest LP 
'Sweet And Sour Tears."

HOLLAN D 
Bovema's Columbia -dept. reports that Cliff Richard and The Shadows will 
be in Holland for the second time in May. Shows will be given in Leeuwarden, 
Scheveningen and Blokker. 
Also on the concert scene will be Atlantic's Charlie Mingus with a sextet on 
Friday night, April 10 in Amsterdam. The Bovema-label already released 
albums such as "The Clown" (available for the first time now) and "Blues 
and Roots." 
Bovema's Stateside label rushed out an EP -recordings of the Metropolitan 
Pops Choir cond. by Robert Mandell, which handles jazz -vocal interpretations, 
of works by J. S. Bach. 
Atlantic will present its 2nd volume of the Ray Charles Story on the Dutch, 
record stands shortly, The Bovema-label also has Ben E. King's "That's When 
It Hurts" on the agenda. 
Grammophonehouse's HMV -label launched The Shepherds' second recording 
"Finito l'Amore"/"Droomland" as a strong follow-up for "Dank U." The trio 
now also has regular broadcasts. 
Adamo is still the no. 1 Hitparade -singer in this country. His "Vous Per- 
mettez Monsieur" is also heading the list of "Tijd Voor Teenagers," one of 
Holland's most popular teen radio shows. 
- 
Liberty's Bobby Vee appeared in AVRO-TV's Scala -show April 1. The 
singer made a visit to Bovema's Grammophonehouse that same day. 
Imperial's vocal star Ronnie Watti has now been signed as vocalist of Vara's 
dance band "The Ramblers." The singer recently made his record debut with 
"Jij Bent Mijn Meisje," a Dutch version of Adamo's "Tombe La Neige." The 
Label's Tiener Top Test -series has been enthusiastically received by dealers and 
musicpress. 
Artone's subsid Funckler Records released the following Reprise albums in 
Benelux: "The Symphonic Ellington" by Duke Ellington, "Treasure of Golden 
Hits" and "Sammy Davis Jr. Salutes The Stars At The London Palladium" by 
Sammy Davis Jr. and "Return To Paradise Island" by Bing Crosby. Both Duke 
and Sammy currently are in the news due to their respective performances in 
Europe. 
Palette Records, distributed by Artone in Benelux, rush -released a strong 
instrumental version of "Non Ho L'Eta" winning song of this year's Eure, 
vision Song Festival. Tune is rendered by Belgium's No. 1 trumpet -player 
Teddy Martens. 
- 
Latest issues from the ABC Paramount line, distributed by Artone, include 
a new Ray Charles LP "Sweet And Sour Tears," an Extended Play selection 
from John Coltrane's "Impressions" and a further extension of the Impulse -line 
with "Illumination" by the Elvin Jones}Jimmy Garrison Sextet. 
- 
The Gordy-Motown-Tamla line has two further U.S. Chart items issued on 
the Benelux market by Artone's subsid ;Funckler Records: Martha & The Van- 
dellas' "Live Wire" and "He's A Good Guy" by The Marvelettes. 
Strong entries from the Aristocrat laine issued by Artone's Funckler Dept. 
are Tommy Tucker's current smash "Hi -Heel Sneakers" and a new LP record, 
ing by Ahmad Jamal entitled "Ahmad Jamal At The Blackhawk." Both platters 
are expected to shape in the Benelux territory.

DENMARK 
The first Danish recordings of the songs from the recent Eurovision Song 
Festival are now available. Pedro Biker has recorded Britain's "I Love The 
Little Things," here titled "Der' No'Et Over Dig," and Finland's "Laiskotellen," 
here titled "Weekend." The Danish lyrics of the British song is written by 
Peter Mynte, and the record is on Philips. Another recent Philips release from 
Nordisk Polyphon Akts. is "Morgen Ist Alles Vorüber"/"Bonjour L'Amour" 
with Ester Marini. Same company has also rushed out Max Roach' "Freedom 
Now Suite." 
When the Copenhagen evening paper B.T. recently published its "most sold 
records during March," it must have been a triumph for EMI which had eight 
of the ten records on that chart. Four of them were with The Beatles. The 
latest released from EMI here includes "Can't Buy Me Love" with The Beatles 
on Parlophone, Cilla Black with "Anyone Who Had A Heart" on the same 
label, "I Love The Little Things" with Matt Monro, "Blue Winter" with Connie 
Francis on MGM and "Twist Im Blut" with Hazy Osterwald Sextet on Colum- 
bia. EPs with Cliff Richard, The Dakotas, Billy J. Kramer and Yves Montand 
were also among the recent releases. 
FINLAND 
The fact that Finland is a country where Finnish language records usually 
do better than foreign language records (and that's unusual, at least in 
Scandinavia) was again documented when Scandia recorded two of The 
Beatles' most popular songs in Finnish. "I Want To Hold Your Hand," here 
titled "Jos Käden Annat Vain" and "From Me To You," here titled "Meidän 
Yhteinen." The single was recorded by Ann -Christine and Johnny with The 
Hounds. 
NORWAY 
Wenche Myhre, 16, local sensation who went to the top of the charts last 
October with her Norwegian reading of the German "Ich Will 'Nen Cowboy 
Als Mann" on Triola, has done it again. This time with a Norwegian song, "La 
Meg Vaere Ung" (Let Me Be Young), one of the songs from the local Song 
Festival this year, and according to many people, the song that should have 
represented Norway at the Eurovision Song Contest in Copenhagen last month. 
Arne Bendiksen, who sang for Norway in Copenhagen, said so before the 
Contest, and after the Contest he repeated it, and'said that with Wenche Myhre 
singing "La Meg Vaere Ung" Norway could very well have created a sensation 
in the Contest. Bendiksen has written and composed this song himself, and as 
head of Egil Monn Iversen A/S in Oslo, he is also the publisher of it. 
The Swedish group The Hootenanny Singers and their "Jag Väntar Vid Min 
Mila" is now being released as single under the Fontana label here, and also as 
LP at the original Polar label. 
Norsk Phonogram A/S (Philips, among others), is now working hard on the 
promotion of Barbra Streisand on CBS in Norway. Same company has also 
released six LPs of the Audio Fidelity label. 
SWEDEN 
1964 looks like the year when every artist finds his way to Sweden, to judge 
from names and touring schedules just published here. A country & western 
group including Chet Atkins, Jim Reeves, Bobby Bare and the Anita Kerr 
Singers is on their way here in the middle of April. Sammy Davis Jr., Alice 
Babs, Ingrid Bergman, Jan Malmsjö, Harry Arnold Orchestra and the Viet- 
namese singer Tiny Young (her real name, Thien Huong Ton Nu Thi is 
considered a little too complicated for a career in European show biz) are 
guests in a charity gala for UNICEF in Stockholm April 25. Charlie Mingus 
and Kenny Ball's Orchestra are contracted for tours in middle of April. Art 
Farmer and Jimmy Hall at the end of April. In beginning of May the Swedes 
can expect Big Dee Irwin and Sound Inc. Michael Cox arrives in middle of May 
and The Dave Clark Five in the end of May. So does Johnny Kidd and The 
Pirates, Cliff Richard, who will continue touring here also in June. In June 
also arrives Woody Herman Orch., and also Jack Dailey, Terry Wayne and 
Jimmy Justice. Gene Vincent and Chubby Checker is also contracted for June. 
Larry Finnegan in June -July, Anita O'Day in July, Ray Charles is also coming 
in July, so does Tex Beneke and the Glenn Miller Orchestra. Around Mid- 
summer we can expect Billy J. Kramer, Adams Faith, Delta Rhythm Boys, 
among others and in end of July Don Gardner and Dee Dee Ford. Mark Murphy 
is contracted for August, Gerry and The Pacemakers, The Swinging Blue Jeans 
and Cilla Black-and eventually, also The Beatles has been mentioned for a 
tour this year. For the latter, no dates or contracts have been fixed yet. Josh 
White, The Brothers Four, Oscar Brown Jr., Oscar Peterson, Ella Fitzgerald, 
Jerry Lee Lewis, Freddie and The Dreamers, Julie Grant and the French 
Johnny Halliday are other names who already are contracted for Swedish tours 
during summer and autumn 1964. Some of the above mentioned will be touring 
Sweden only, while others are contracted for all -Scandinavian tours. 
Britain's "I Love The Little Things," second in the Eurovision Song Contest 
last month, is titled "Bara Ett Litet Ord" in Swedish. Sonora Musikförlags AB 
is rushing out the sheet music with Swedish lyrics by Bengt Sten. According 
to Sture Borgedahl of Sonora, the first Swedish recordings can be expected 
any day now. 
Philips -Sonora has rushed out two EPs with the local group Spiralerna (The 
Spirals), who made their TV debut last Good Friday singing negro spirituals. 
Among actual record releases here can be mentioned "Four Days That 
Shocked The World" on Colpix, rushed out here by Sonet Grammofon AB. 
Of records from the Eurovision Song Contest has been released here the 
British "I Love The Little Things" with Matt Monro on Parlophone, the 
German "Man Gewöhnt Sich So Schnell An Das Schöne" with Nora Nova on 
Ariola, the French "Le Chant de Mallory" with Rachel on Barclay and, of 
course, the winning Italian "Non Ho L'Eta" with Gioliola Cinquetti on Triola. 
Publisher Stig Anderson (and Mrs. Anderson) off for Paris, Madrid and 
Canary Islands for two weeks of combined business and vacation trip. 
Restaurant Ambassadeur in Stockholm changed owners on April 1, with 
Börge Bruun, already running the PB in Stockholm's Old Town and Restaurant 
Peter Mynde as the new owner of Ambassadeur. For the coming summer, the 
restaurant will operate as a night-club, but for the autumn certain changes 
were announced. It is expected that the restaurant might try to specialize in 
local artistes, mainly record artistes. It seems obvious that striptease acts, 
popular on every spot here a couple of years ago, are not longer interesting 
the audiences.

$30 FIRST CLASS-$45 AIR MAIL 
Frankie Laine arrived in Tokyo on April 1, and attended a press conference 
held at Hotel Okura the next day. He expressed his pleasure of realizing his 
plan of coming to Japan, which he had in mind for seven years. 
Nippon Grammophon is releasing a new standard size (12") stereo LP 
series on April 20, chiefly featuring Japanese and foreign popular songs, 
instrumentals, movie themes in various new arrangements. The first release 
is five disks, including "Wakare Bune" (Guitar of Harumi Ibe), "Tennessee 
Waltz" (trumpet of Shiro Onda) and "Latin, Hawaiian Album" (by Ginji 
Yamaguchi and others). 
Yukio Hashi, the songster of Nippon Victor, will attend the opening show 
of the newly built New Auditorium in Hawaii on May 29 and 30 under the 
auspices of the Yukio Hashi Fan Club of Hawaii. (Going with him are Akemi 
Misawa and Aiko Ito. 
Toshiba Records is releasing three special disks in late April in response 
to the popularity of the Beatles here, "Can't Buy My Love," "You Can't Do 
That," "From Me To You," "I Saw Her Standing There," "Twist And Shout," 
"Roll Over Beethoven." The Beatles are reported as having a wish to visit 
Japan on their way back from their tour in Australia around the end of June.

POP BEST BETS 
"CABIN IN THE SKY"-New York Cast Pro- 
duction-Capitol SW 2073 
The revival of the classic 1940 musical didn't 
make the Off-B'way grade in its recent revival, 
but that certainly wasn't the fault of the 
engaging Vernon Duke -John Latouche score. The 
show music coterie will be grateful to Capitol 
for making a post -run release of the revival cast 
album, even if "Cabin in the Sky" in a recording 
studio is not quite the spirited household it was 
on stage. The great songs: "Cabin in the Sky," 
"Do What You Want to Do," 'We'll Live All 
Over Again," "Not a Care in the World" and 
"Taking A Chance On Love." 
"SENTIMENTAL GUITAR"-Tony Mattola- 
Command RS 864 SD 
Tony Mattola scored a substantial chart success 
with his while -back offering, "Romantic Guitar," 
and this new issue on Command is loaded with 
the same good listening ingredients. With some 
moodful and lilting backdrop accompaniment, the 
guitarist takes a smooth lyrical approach on the 
melodies on such old favorites as "In A Senti- 
mental Mood," "If I Had You," "In The Wee 
Small Hours Of The Morning" and 
9 other 
equally melodic items. Eye it for brisk sales. 
"WHITE LIGHTNING!"-Jerry White-Monu- 
ment MLP 8016 
Here's a bright and bouncy package of evergreens 
plus one recent item served up in tinkling razma- 
tazz style by Jerry White on Monument. The 
88'er injects plenty of that "old barroom" flavor 
as he lashes out with a nimble -fingered talent that 
proves a natural for "Sweet Georgia Brown," 
"Bill Bailey," "Maple Leaf Rag" and seven other 
equally melodic tunes. Lots of nostalgia to be had 
here. 
"THE WHISTLER & 
HIS GUITAR"-Toots 
Thielemans-ABC Paramount 482 
Toots Thielemans displays a whole lot of instru- 
mental talent on this new offering from ABC 
Paramount as he whistles to the accompaniment 
of his own guitar. The guitarist, who made a bit 
of noise with a recent single tagged, "Bluesette," 
includes it in this set of mood melodies served up 
in pop -jazz fashion. Superb listening throughout 
as the whistler reads "Wives And Lovers," "It's 
Only A Paper Moon" and "Deep Purple." 
"50 FABULOUS HAWAIIAN FAVORITES"- 
Leroy Holmes-United Artists 6353 
Here's another from UA's "50 Fabulous Favorite" 
series, this time featuring the talents of Leroy 
Holmes and the Southwinds. The orkster and his 
crew briefly breeze through a host of Island 
melodies spiced with throbbing rhythms and 
swaying guitars. Included here are "Hawaiian 
War Chant," "It Happened In Kaloha," "My 
Little Grass Shack," "Down Along The Sheltering 
Palms" and many others. Much pleasant listening 
to be had here. 
"LI'L DARLIN' "-Neal Hefti-20th Century - 
Fox TFM 3139 
The multi -talented Neal Hefti displays the com- 
posing side of his versatile musical coin on this 
top-drawer set of originals from 20th Century - 
Fox. Hefti has also arranged all the jazz -flavored 
selections here and has presented them in a lush 
strings -oriented 
orchestral 
setting. 
Standout 
tracks here include "Should I Or Shouldn't I," 
"Late Date" and "Nice To Be With You." Deejays 
should find loads of programmable material on 
the disk. 
"FLAMENCO 
CONCERT"-Carlos Montoya- 
RCA Victor LSP 2846 
The rare, distinctive flamenco artistry of Carlos 
Montoya is superbly showcased here in a delight- 
ful program of familiar guitar classics. Montoya's 
personal brand of musicanship blends different 
style into one cohesive musical element. The 
artist shines on "Farruca," "Jots" and as extra 
treat, "Blues In The Night" played in the fla- 
menco style. A magnificent achievement.

######## cb 1964-05-02 p50  [mingus]
DENMARK 
The Beatles are coming to Copenhagen for two concerts at the KB-Hall on 
June 4. They are the most expensive artists ever presented in Denmark, but 
the arranger refuses to say how expensive. The KB-Hall is the biggest spot in 
Scandinavia for such events, taking 4400 people at each performance. 
The Danish Music Dealers' Association celebrated its 60th birthday on April 
13. A reception was held at Hotel Richmond in Copenhagen. 
"Sangen Om Dig," this year's Danish Eurovision Song Festival entry, re- 
corded by Bjorn Tidmand, has been released on Parlophone in Great Britain. 
Dansk Gramofonpladeforlag (Sonet, among others) has taken over Supra- 
phon for Denmark, Karl Emil Knudsen, head of the company, told Cash Box. 
The Czech label has a very strong catalog of classic recordings, of which there 
is a great demand in Denmark with an estimated sale of 30 to 35% of all rec- 
ords being sold belonging to the classical category. 
Poul Bundgaard has recorded two of this year's Eurovision songs for Tono, 
both in Danish. It is "Sporg Ikke, Hvorfor ...," the Austrian entry "Warum, 
Nur Warum," and "Den Forbudne Frugt" being Monaco's "Ou Sont -Elles 
Passees." Inge Ostergaard, a new name on Tono, has done the French entry, 
"Sangen Om Mallory" (Le Chant De Mallory), in Danish, b/w "Jeg Vil Danse" 
(Bright And Shiny), Erik 011gaard of Tono told Cash Box. 
Ester Ofarim and Abraham came to Copenhagen for radio and p.a. April 17 
and 18. Of other artists from the Philips stable who have been in Copenhagen 
recently can be mentioned Anita Lindblom who came here to make a TV show 
that will represent Denmark at this year's Montreux TV Festival. Johnny 
Griffin, recording for Riverside, has done very well at Copenhagen's jazz spot 
Montmartre. Modern Jazz Quartet has just been in Copenhagen, so has Charlie 
Mingus. Of recent releases, Owe Wiisholm of Nordisk Polyphon Nkst (NPA) 
particularly mentioned "Move Cver Darling" with Doris Day on CBS and "I'm 
On Fire" with Jerry Lee Lewis on Philips. On Mercury has just been released 
the album "Roland Kirk Quartet meets the Benny Golson Orchestra." 
H. Rosenlow Jensen, label manager of Decca at NPA told Cash Box that 
Jorn Grauengaard has just signed a contract with NPA and will be recording 
for the Decca label, where a serial of Danish recordings has just started. Katy 
Bodtger has made the French "Le Chant De Mallory" in Danish on Polydor. 
Terry Stafford's "Suspicion" on London and Dana Valery's English language 
version of this year's Eurovision Song Contest winner, the Italian "Non Ho 
L'Eta" (This Is My Prayer) on Decca are recent releases from which the com- 
pany expects a lot in the next weeks. 
Decca in Denmark has a very strong catalog of classic music this spring, 
it was learned. Also on the jazz field, NPA has a strong position, among others 
at the Verve label with Ella Fitzgerald's album "These Are The Blues," and a 
series of ten EPs with top names in jazz. 
Imudico A/S is Danish publisher of Monaco's Eurovision entry this year, 
"Ou Sont -Elles Passees," in Danish titled "Den Forbudne Frugt" (The For- 
bidden Fruit) with Danish lyrics by Ase Gjodsbol-Krogh. Another Imudico re- 
lease, "I Only Want To Be With You" has been recorded in Danish by Gui- 
tarpigerne (The Guitar Girls) at Columbia. 
NORWAY 
Corning up very strong here now is Gigliola Cinquetti on Triola with the 
winning Eurovision Contest song "Non Ho L'Eta," this week entering the 
charts in the tenth spot. Local talent Wenche Myhre continue topping the chart 
with her Triola recording of "La Meg Vaere Ung" (Let Me Be Young). 
Iversen & Frogh A/S, the EMI distributor in Norway, is expecting a lot 
from a religious record, "It's An Open Secret"/"We're Going To Set The 
World A Singing" with The Joy Strings, a Salvation Army Band, on the Re- 
gal label. 
Arne Bendiksen, who recently took over Egil Monn Iversen A/S, is planning 
to change the name of the company to Arne Bendiksen A/S, it was reported 
to Cash Box.

Local Stockholm daily evening paper Aftonbladet recently gave a w 
page to describe the situation in record biz vs. Swedish Broadcasting Co. î 
very critical article noted that since about three years, all record sales 
Sweden is more or less dictated by about 400 youths, many of which are 
than teenagers, some of them being only nine years old. Every Sat 
SBC has a program in which these 400 vote about "most popular recordi 
not necessarily the same as "most sold records." However, since it's the s 
popular program among teenagers, the tendency among record retailer 
Sweden is that if a record is not appearing among the ten or 15 played or 
program, no retailer keeps it in stock "it is useless since no one will eve, 
for it." The program, "Tio I Topp" (Ten In The Top) has been aired 130 t 
in 127 times produced and guided by Klas Burling, who no doubt knr 
lot about music and pop records, but also a person who has his own far 
among pop artists. Judging from his programs, an artist has to be Brit, 
he has any chance to be aired on Burling's programs. There are some :t 
lations for the Tio-I-Topp programs. Among others it is stipulated that 
one under 12 shall appear as a jury member (Aftonbladet lists three who 
only nine and ten who were only eleven years old); it is also stipulated 
no one shall be allowed to be a jury member more than maximum four 
this to avoid that too much of one person's individual taste shall dom 
the program (Aftonbladet list names of several teenagers who have op 
as jury member between 30 and 55 weeks).

Pick of the Week 
VIVA LAS VEGAS (2:13) 
[Elvis Presley BMI-Pomus, 
Shuman] 
ELVIS PRESLEY (RCA Victor 8360) 
Once again a Presley deck hits the wax mart and, once again, it means 
money -in -the -bank for all concerned. Both sides are in Elvis' latest 
flick, "Viva Las Vegas," and both should be on their way in no time flat. 
One end, featuring the Jordanaires, is the pit's title tune that sports 
the excitement of that fabulous city. The other's a sizzling revival of the 
Ray Charles' classic, "What'd I Say," that has the Jubilee Four & The 
Lombard Qt. colorfully assisting. 
WHAT'D I SAY (3:03) 
[Progressive BMI-Charles] 
EVERYBODY KNOWS (2:35) [Gil BMI-Duncan, Reed] 
ONE LOVE TOO LATE (2:20) [Maxana ASCAP-Velona] 
STEVE LAWRENCE (Columbia 43047) 
The pro performer never sounded better than he does on his newest 
Columbia platter. Steve's hushed -voice, (partly) multi -tracked reading 
is a treat to the ear on the lovely, soft cha cha beat romantic weeper 
tabbed "Everybody Knows." Superb string -filled ork-choral showcase sup- 
plied by Bob Mersey. Marion Evans turns in a top back-up job on the 
warm hallad heat, "One Love Too Late." 
CHOOSE (2:50) 
BEE-BOM (2:10) 
[Gil BMI-Bart] 
[Mills ASCAP-Vandyke] 
SAMMY DAVIS, JR. (Reprise 0278) 
The fantastic talent can soon add another pair of disk triumphs to his 
collection. This powerful two-sided follow-up to "Shelter Of Your Arms" 
can be all over the charts in the weeks to come. One end, "Choose," is 
a meaningfully beautiful, build -to -a -big -finish romantic ballad (penned 
by Lionel "Oliver" Bart) that Sammy and the Jimmie Haskell ork- 
choral outfit put across in dramatically effective fashion. On the other 
end Sammy and Chuck Sagle's crew happily knock out a contagious, 
finger-snappin' novelty tabbed "Bee -Born." 
BIG BOSS LINE (2:40) [Merrimac BMI-Tucker] 
BE MY GIRL (2:25) [Merrimac BMI-Tucker, Wilson] 
JACKIE WILSON (Brunswick 55266) 
Wilson can climb back aboard the hit bandwagon with this new Bruns- 
wick stint. Leadoff portion's a wild, hard-hitting rocker, tabbed "Big Boss 
Line," that features Jackie at his enthusiastic best. Red-hot support 
from the Gil Askey-led ork-choral group. Companion piece is a tantaliz- 
ing, hip -swinging beat -ballad romancer tabbed "Be My Girl." 
RULES OF LOVE (2:35) [Kalmann ASCAP-Mann, Appell] 
HEARTBREAK HOTEL (2:30) [Tree BMI-Axton, Durden, Presley] 
THE ORLONS (Cameo 319) 
,Check the charts in the near future for the Orlons' latest Cameo 
stand. It's a pounding rock novelty, tabbed "Rules Of Love," that takes 
a throbbing "What'd I Say" route. Great instrumental backing has a 
crowd cheering the artists on. Underlid's a soulful rock -a -rhythmic up- 
dating of Elvis Presley's initial giant. Dandy two-sider. 
LET'S GO TOGETHER (2:35) [Trio BMI-Barry, Greenwich] 
YOU GOT WHAT I LIKE (2:10) [T. M. BMI-Greenwich] 
THE RAINDROPS (Jubilee 5475) 
The Raindrops, who just completed another solid chart run (with the 
Idie, "Book Of Love"), can head right back to money -making territory 
-this time aboard a newie tabbed "Let's Go Together." Tune, penned 
by prolific tunesmiths Jeff Barry & Ellie Greenwich, is a bright jumper 
that's right up the teeners' alley. Side's loaded with chart -making vocal 
and musical ingredients. Also keep close tabs on the tasty twist'er "You 
Got What I Like." It's got what the kids like. 
HICKORY, DICK AND DOC (2:27) [Fred Rose BMI-Blackwell] 
I WISH YOU WERE MINE AGAIN (2:22) 
[Saima BMI-Velline, Lesslie] 
BOBBY VEE (Liberty 55700) 
Vee, who's coming off a winning entry in "I'll Make You Mine," makes 
another strong bid for more chart laurels with this new Liberty slice. 
It's a tantalizing, multi -track cha cha beat affair about three fellas, 
named "Hickory, Dick and Doc," who chased the same gal-running after 
her like 'three blind mice.' Stellar Bill Justis ork-choral assist. Ernie 
Freeman and the Johnny Mann Singers expertly back up on the very 
pretty, up tempo shuffle beat sentimental ballad coupler. 
HAPPY TEENAGER (2:16) 
[Stacy BMI-Margo, Margo, Medress, Siegel] 
DRY YOUR EYES (2:30) 
[Bright Tunes BMI-Margo, Margo, Medress, Siegel] 
RANDY & THE RAINBOWS (Rust 5080) 
Randy & The Rainbows, who had a potent coin -catcher with their 
session devoted to "Denise," can be in for more of the same with this 
newie about a "Happy Teenager." Side's a sparkling, handclapping 
chock full of teen -appealing vocal and instrumental tricks. In- 
viting undercut's the Tokens' oldie that Randy & Co. run thru at a quick 
beat clip. 
C mediocre 
Pick of the Week 
THE COURT OF KING CARACTUS (2:19) 
[Beechwood BMI-Arr: Harris] 
TWO BUFFALOS (2:46) [Eastlake ASCAP-Hyman] 
ROLF HARRIS (Epic 9682) 
The Australian hit -maker can have another one of those infectious nov- 
elty clicks with this delectable entry. Tagged "The Court Of King Carac- 
tus," it's an up tempo ditty that adds a line and picks up steam each 
time around. Fetching wobble -effect in the backdrop. "Two Buffalos" 
takes a toe-tappin' ride on the catchy flip. 
SECURITY (2:30) [East -Time BMI-Redding] 
I WANT TO THANK YOU (2:35) [East -Time BMI-Redding] 
OTIS REDDING (Volt 117) 
Otis Redding, who hit last time out with "Come To Me," seems des- 
tined to go a like pop-r&b success route with this newie tagged "Secur- 
ity." The tune is a hard -driving full ork-backed blues lament with a con- 
tagious, junky rapidly -changing chromatic pattern. The flip, "I Want 
To Thank You," is a medium -paced happy romancer essayed with au- 
thority and poise by the chanter. 
BEG ME (2:37) [T. M. BMI-Clark] 
FOR ALL TIME (2:40) [Damic, Zann BMI-Green, Jackson] 
CHUCK JACKSON (Wand 154) 
Jackson's a cinch to add another potent coin -catcher to his long list 
of credits with this new Wand release. Side to eye is the thumping, up 
tempo wailer, "Beg Me," that Chuck and his combo -choral support work 
up into a soul -filled frenzy a number of times along the way. Exciting 
session that can take right off. Backing's an ear -pleasing cha cha beat 
love affair. 
WE WERE LOVERS (WHEN THE PARTY BEGAN) (2:01) 
[Trio BMI-Fisher, Powers] 
HAVING MY FUN (1:56) [Sylvia BMI-Reid, Rooney] 
THE EXCITERS (United Artists 721) 
The Exciters can have their most important chart date since their 
fabulous success with "Tell Him." Side's a tear -compelling rock -a -cha-cha 
affair, tabbed "We Were Lovers (When The Party Began)," that the 
artists serve up in ultra -commercial fashion. Terrific Artie Butler ar- 
rangement and effective choral gimmick on a deck with bust -wide-open 
potential. However, don't overlook sock rock -a -shuffle swinger, "Having 
My Fun." It, too, can come thru. 
NEW YORK WORLD'S FAIR (2:20) [Rhinelander BMI-Harrison] 
MAMA, MAMA, MAMA (2:15) [Excellorec BMI-Arr: Redd] 
WILBUR HARRISON (Constellation 122) 
Harrison is back in the "Kansas City" groove and it looks (and 
sounds) like he has another big winner on his hands. This time, how- 
ever, he's heading towards the "New York World's Fair" and he's doing 
so in a delightful thump -rock fashion a la "Kansas City." Wilbur turns 
in another dandy rock -a -rhythmic job on the "Mama, Mama, Mama" flip. 
Can be a double-header. 
Newcomer Picks 
DON'T LET THE SUN CATCH 
PM THE ONE (2:16) 
YOU CRYING (2:33) 
Pacemaker BMI-Marsden] 
[Pacemaker BMI-Marsden] 
GERRY & THE PACEMAKERS (Laurie 3251) 
Chances are Gerry & The Pacemakers will be the next big English 
group to be making the U.S. chart scene. Fellas, due here soon for ap- 
pearances on the Ed Sullivan TV'er, are currently riding the lists in 
England with one end, "Don't Let The Sun Catch You Crying." It's an 
extremely pretty soft Latin beat romancer that really grows on you 
with each listen. "I'm The One," on the other end, is a previously -re- 
leased English hit. It's a solid foot-stomp'er that can also break big here. 
WHO CARES WHAT PEOPLE SAY (2:39) 
[Rittenhouse BMI-Raleigh, Meade] 
MY JOHNNY DOESN'T COME AROUND (2:19) 
[Picturetone BMI-Taylor, Richards, Farrell] 
DEBBIE ROLLINS (Ascot 2150) 
Debbie Rollins, who clicked territorially last time out with "He Really 
Loves Me," can go all the way up the national charts with this potent 
Ascot newie tagged "Who Cares What People Say." The tune is a me- 
dium -paced, chorus -backed soulful pop -blues affair about a gal who 
makes up her mind to stick with her guy in spite of gossip. The attrac- 
tive undercut, "My Johnny Doesn't Come Around," is a slow -moving. 
shuffle -beat tradition -styled r&b weeper read with authority by the lark. 
DOES YOUR HEART HURT A LITTLE (2:26) 
[Ludlow BMI-Christopher, Lombardo] 
I'M A FOOL (TO GO ON LOVING YOU) (2:11) 
[Champion BMI-Martin] 
BOBBI MARTIN (Coral 62410) 
Bobbi Martin could have the 'stepping stone' she's been seeking via her 
newest Coral effort. Thrush's fine vocal stylings come across with touch- 
ing sincerity as she carves out the heartfelt ballad, "Does Your Hears 
Hurt A Little." Excellent Nashville -flavored choral-ork showcase. Under 
lid's a tender, tear -compelling shuffle -ballad original-with country over 
tones.

PASSWORD (2:30) [Kitty Wells BMI-Phillips] 
I'VE THOUGHT OF LEAVING YOU (2:41) [Marizona BMI-Emerson] 
KITTY WELLS (Decca 31622) 
Kitty Wells, who is currently riding the charts with "This White Cit. 
de On My Finger," comes up with a potent follow-up stanza with this 
offering. The top side, "Password," is an easy-going, shufflin' ode all 
about the hardships of playing the "game" of love. The coupler, "I've 
Thought Of Leaving You," is a contagious, chorus -backed honk tonic. 
styled affair about a gal whose guy is cheating. 
TOO MANY IRONS IN THE FIRE (2:09) [Pamper BMI-Howard] 
I LEANED OVER BACKWARDS FOR YOU (2:44) 
[Pamper BMI-Howard] 
"LITTLE" JIMMY DICKENS (Columbia 43040) 
"Little" Jimmy Dickens has enough things going for himself with this 
newie labeled "Too Many Irons In The Fire" to reach the charts in nn 
time flat. The side's a rousing, uptempo, chorus -backed item about a gal 
who plays a large romantic field. The attractive undercut, "I Leaned 
Over Backwards For You," is a slow -moving, shuffle -beat bluegrass. 
styled traditional tear-jerker. 
CLEOPATRA (2:19) [Hastings BMI-Howard] 
MALINDA (2:43) [Acuff -Rose BMI-Kershaw] 
RUSTY & DOUG (RCA Victor 8362) 
The vet country songsters can quickly strike paydirt with this new 
ultra -commercial Victor tabbed "Cleopatra." The tune is a medium -paced. 
hard -driving historical lament all about the famed ancient vamp. Dee - 
jays should come out in force for the side. The flip, "Malinda," is a lively, 
high-powered romancer with a contagious south -of -the -border beat. 
HOLD MY HURT FOR AWHILE (2:33) [English BMI-Poovey] 
JOHN SAID (2:10) [Tree BMI-Stover] 
BOBBY BARNETT (Sims 177) 
Bobby Barnett has been running hot lately and he should zoom up 
the charts again with this potent new Sims entry tabbed "Hold bly 
Hurt For Awhile." The side is an easy-going, medium -paced, chorus - 
backed lament delivered with loads of sincerity by the artist. The 
coupler, "John Said," is a rollicking, uptempo romantic novelty in th. 
best country tradition. 
BIG JOHN'S WIFE (3:00) [Acuff -Rose BMI-Carver, Abner] 
PIRATE KING [Starday BMI-Masters] 
WILMA LEE & STONEY COOPER (Hickory 1257) 
Wilma and Stoney can get back in their chart -riding ways with thin 
splendid item called "Big John's Wife." Tune is a pulsating, chorus 
backed rhythmic tale about the problems of life on bayou. Plenty of Po- 
tential here. "Pirate King" is a lively, uptempo romantic ditty concern- 
ing a bygone ladies' man. Also merits a close look.

A three-day international sales meeting took place at Fontana Records' 
central offices in Baarn recently. Plans were worked out for the 1964-1965 
season concerning the Riverside and Pacific Jazz repertoire distributed by 
Fontana in all major markets outside the USA and Canada. The label's sales 
promoters from Belgium, Britain, France, Germany, Holland and Italy con- 
vened in Baarn for the occasion. Present as special guests were Orin Keep - 
news (who heads Riverside operations in the States) and Alan Bates of Inter - 
disk. It was learned that among the items were forthcoming campaigns for 
major talent represented on the labels, among them Cannonball Adderley, 
Art Blakey, Charlie Byrd, Thelonious Monk and Wes Montgomery. 
N.V. Bovema reports some miscellaneous news from its dynamic bunch of U.S. 
labels: Liberty now brings up a collector's item by the late Eddie Cochran, 
still very much in demand in this area. Columbia, from its Epic -catalog, re- 
leased Bobby Vinton's "My Heart Belongs To Only You." Capitol launched 
two excellent LP -albums by Peggy Lee (In Love Again) and Nat King Cole 
(Let's Face The Music). 
The forthcoming Holland Festival 1964 will feature several Bovema/EMI- 
artists: Carlo Maria Giulini, Kubelik, Klemperer, Dietrich Fischer Dieskau, 
Elisabeth Schwartzkopf, Sviatoslav Richter, George Szell and Herbert von 
Karajan. 
Imperial -news this week: Cor Steyn recently featured his Magic Organ in 
the TV -series "Pas Geperst." Steyn recorded two of the best Adamo -hits, 
"Amour Perdu" and "Tombe La Neige." The label also rushed out "Mr. Clari- 
net," an album by the Ad van den Hoed Quartet and guest singer Francis v. 
Rooy. 
Johnny Jordaan, now celebrating his 25th anniversary as a singer, appeared 
in Willem O'Duys' TV -show "Voor de Vuist Weg," introducing his latest re- 
cording "Toon Mij Je Hart." 
Further Adamo -news: Adamo drew enthusiastic audiences in Eindhoven on 
April 12 last and has also been signed for one niters in the Hague (May 17) 
and Tilburg (May 18). Bovema steadily provides dealers with Adamo -display- 
material. 
Adamo's recent appearance in AVRO's-program "Voor de Vuist Weg" 
caused so many positive reactions all over the country, that the show conse- 
quently had to be repeated, a seldom occurring event in Holland! 
Bovema's Imperial -label released two important jazz -LP's "The Great Les- 
ter Young," featuring collector's items by the late tenor saxist. Arie van Veen, 
who became a TV -personality in TV -trials of late, has been inked by Imperial; 
accordion group The Galanti's made a single record in the sign of the recent 
Johnny Jordaan-jubilee. 
Henk Elsink got rave reviews for his last TV -show on Sunday, April 19. 
The singer's now on his way to a working -vacation in Spain. 
Imperial's "Music For You" series celebrates its 1st anniversary. A num- 
ber of 28 albums have been released so far, all in all achieving these series 
to be the cheapest and most frequently reviewed in Holland. 
Sky high on th British Hitparade are Peter & Gordon, whose "World With- 
out Love," accompanied by Geoff Love's Orchestra, has also been rushed out 
by Bovema's Columbia -label. 
Gramophonehouse's Imperial -chief Cees Mentink reports that Bovema will 
again organize its 2nd Kaag Talent -Contests at Warmond in the course of 
June and July next. There will be separate sections for rock, jazz and miscel- 
laneous. Paul Acket's "Muziek Expres" will co-operate on the project. 
Trumpeter Gerard Engelsma recorded "Posthorn -Twist" for Imperial. Bo- 
vema's Stateside label has Diane Renay out with "Kiss Me Sailor." 
Capitol -Holland will hit the stands with three special -coupled EP -recordings 
by George Shearing, featuring highlights from his latest LP -jazz -concerts. 
The Beach Boys' "Fun, Fun, Fun" is a steady seller. 
The Jumping Jewels and singer Johnny Lion, Philips -artists and winners 
of Holland's Popularity Polls 1962 and 1963, will tour Singapore and other 
places in the Orient. Accompanied by their most competent and diligent man- 
ager Herman Batelaan of the Hague, the five young men (average age is 21) 
left Thursday, April 23, from Schiphol Airport, Amsterdam. Busloads of fans 
were present, intending to present their idol Johnny Lion with a new-born cub 
from Circus Boltini. In the past, the Dutch vocal duo The Blue Diamonds, fe- 
male Dutch star Anneke Grönloh and the Band of the Dutch Swing College 
have scored fantastic successes in Malaya of almost royal airs. Miss C. Keeler, 
in charge for Philips Records Singapore, has started a large publicity -cam- 
paign for the Jumping Jewels and Johnny Lion, making front-page news in 
advance. The singer and his instrumental group have over a dozen hits and 
two LP -albums selling fast in the Dutch market. 
Fine response in Holland for the American group The Serendipity Singers, 
the 9 -piece instrumental and folk -singing students, released here on the Phil- 
ips label. Otto Vriezenberg of Phonogram told Cash Box that "Don't Let The 
Rain Come Down" (Crooked little man) c/w "Freedom Star" has all the po- 
tentialities for a fine start. Although radio -plugging and publicity have started 
quite satisfactorily, he pleads, of course, for a personal appearance of the 
group in Europe. 
Teresa Brewer's new contract with Mercury means releases of her new re- 
cordings on the Philips label here, promoted by Philips' Phonographic Indus- 
tries at Baarn. Her come-back is single "Come On In" c/w "Simple Things." 
A Dutch translation of Aznavour s "La Mamma," the song devoted to the 
Queen of the Gypsies, was recorded in Holland by Connie Brokken on the Phil- 
ips -label. The song was plugged intensively (also in Miss Brokken's own TV - 
show) and is growing out to a tremendous success. Miss Brokken is once 
more in the Top Ten of a Dutch hit-parade. 
Dixieland -group The New Orleans Syncopaters of Amsterdam, led by pian- 
ist Jan Burgers, made a hit in this country of "Washington Square." They 
continue this successful trend with "Come Friends," based on an old Flemish 
folk-song, also with a banjo -introduction leading to a smooth and swinging 
Dixie -improvisation on Decca. 
Terry Stafford's "Suspicion" was rush -released by John Ros of Phonogram 
on the London label. The hit gets intense plugging, going every half hour for 
commercial radio and was tipped by officials for the top five. On Fontana, 
Millie of Jamaica sings Blue Beat songs, of which "My Boy Lollipop" is an- 
other candidate for the Dutch top -scores.
